# afs/

Annual Financial Statements engine — IFRS / IFRS-for-SMEs packs (BS/IS/CF/notes) from GL, renders to HTML/DOCX/PDF, review workflow, portal delivery. Largest single module (42 files).

## Modules
- **Document + version**: `afsDocumentService.ts` (a "document" = one year × company), `afsSectionService.ts` (20+ ordered sections), `afsSectionAttestation.ts` (the section write guard), `afsVersionHistoryService.ts`, `afsGenerationJobService.ts` (async job queue `queued → running → complete|failed`), `afsTypes.ts` (re-exports `afsKpiTypes.ts`, `afsPortalTypes.ts`, `afsComplianceTypes.ts`).
- **Mapping**: `afsMappingService.ts` — COA → AFS line mapping.
- **Note engine**: `noteEngineService.ts` (4-stage: fetch → generate → suppress → persist), `noteDataQueryService.ts`, `noteTemplateRegistry.ts`, `noteRendererService.ts`, `noteAiService.ts` (AI narrative for qualitative), `noteGenerators/` (one file per note: PPE, intangibles, tax, leases…).
- **Statement calculators**: `cashFlowDirectService.ts`, `cashFlowReconciliationService.ts`, `changesInEquityService.ts`, `pisCalculatorService.ts` (Public Interest Score — Companies Act reg 26 → audit/review/compiled), `kpiScorecardService.ts`.
- **Rendering / export**: `afsHtmlRendererService.ts`, `afsHtmlCoverTemplates.ts`, `afsHtmlTableRenderer.ts`, `docxExportService.ts`, `docxTableRenderer.ts`, `pdfExportService.ts`, `weasyprintService.ts` (Python WeasyPrint HTTP service), `serverChartSvg.ts`, `casewareExportExtService.ts`.
- **Branding / templates**: `brandProfileService.ts`, `imageLibraryService.ts`, `reportTemplates.ts`, `entityTerminology.ts` (Company/CC/Trust label swap).
- **Review workflow**: `afsReviewService.ts` (section review/sign-off), `afsDocumentTransitions.ts` (submit / promote / sign off, each under the document's row lock), `afsReviewError.ts` + `afsReviewErrorResponse.ts` (one refusal type and one HTTP mapping: 404 wrong document, 409 locked/contended, 403 impersonated), `afsSectionCommentService.ts`, `afsPreExportChecks.ts` (blocker gate).
- **Proof / signing**: `afsProofCopyService.ts`, `signumIntegrationService.ts` (e-signature), `afsSigningIntegrity.ts` (content fingerprint + refusal), `cipcFilingGuideService.ts`.
- **Compliance**: `complianceCheckerService.ts` (IFRS structural/mathematical/disclosure checks), `complianceAlertService.ts`.
- **Management pack**: `managementPackConfigService.ts`, `managementPackGeneratorService.ts`, `packAiSummaryService.ts`, `packSchedulerService.ts`, `packDeliveryService.ts`.
- **Portal (client-facing review/approval)**: `portalContactsService.ts`, `magicLinkService.ts` (30-min single-use tokens), `portalNotificationService.ts`.

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/afs/*` and `pages/api/portal/afs/*`. Every public function takes `companyId` first (or documentId+companyId). `weasyprintService` shells out over HTTP to a separate Python service.

## Main function signatures
- `enqueueGenerationJob(companyId, documentId, userId): Promise<AfsGenerationJob>` / `markJobStarted / markJobComplete`.
- `generateSection(companyId, documentId, sectionKey): Promise<AfsSection>` / `generateAllSections(...)` — note-engine orchestrator.
- `markSectionReviewed / signOffSection / submitDocumentForReview(companyId, documentId, userId)`.
- `getCashFlowDirect(companyId, yearStart, yearEnd)` — direct-method cash flow.
- `runComplianceCheck(companyId, documentId)` — IFRS structural/math/disclosure.
- `createMagicLink(contactId, documentId): Promise<{ token }>` / `verifyMagicLink(token)` — single-use, 30-min expiry, atomic consume.
- `deliverPack(documentId, companyId)` / `scheduleDelivery(companyId, documentId, config)`.

## Business rules
- Section order and keys are fixed in `reportTemplates` / `noteTemplateRegistry`. Add new notes via `noteGenerators/` + registry entry.
- Document state machine: `draft → review → approved → issued`; `afsPreExportChecks` runs before `issued` and blocks on imbalances / missing mandatory notes.
- PIS calculator drives outcome (audit/review/compiled) — required before generation.
- Magic-link tokens are single-use and consumed atomically inside `verifyMagicLink` (UPDATE…RETURNING with `used_at IS NULL` guard).
- Portal contacts are a separate auth path — magic link only, no password; tenant scope enforced by joining `portal_contacts.company_id`.
- WeasyPrint runs out-of-process — handle timeouts; large packs may hit connection reset.
- Version history: every generation snapshots the rendered output so earlier drafts are recoverable; callers NEVER overwrite in place.
- A document transition takes `lockDocumentForTransition` (FOR UPDATE) BEFORE counting its sections, and its UPDATE repeats the status it decided on. Never count first: a section write in flight would commit unseen behind the transition's own UPDATE.
- Generation is a section write like any other: `generateSection(companyId, documentId, sectionId, fiscalYear, framework, userId)` locks and voids before it writes, and `POST /generate` is refused while the document is out for signature.
- A document with `signing_requested_at` set is locked to section writes (comments excepted — see below). The signing fingerprint covers exactly the values the render prints — the period/fiscal year, the registered company name and number, the branding the CSS and cover use (or the marker for `DEFAULT_BRAND_PROFILE`, used when a company has saved none: nothing creates one at company creation), and each section's id, type, content, overrides, chart data and sort_order (the render prints sections in that ORDER, no number) — and nothing the render never prints (footer, document type, framework, review status, draft AI narrative). **The logo is covered by its URL, not its image**: Signum fetches the image itself, so the picture behind an unchanged URL is not attested. The pre-image is jsonb text (NULL distinct from '', strings quoted) — a single expression in `afsSigningIntegrity.ts`; no migration copies it — with a per-input digest so the refusal names the input that changed; company and brand edits stay allowed while a document is out for signature; `withSignatureImpactWarnings` wraps each such write (tenant settings, brand PUT, admin rename), takes the affected documents' digests before and after it in the same transaction, and warns for exactly the documents whose company or brand digest changed — no field list exists outside `afsSigningIntegrity.ts`. Accepted over-inclusions, reachable only out of band: sort_order values (a renumber that keeps order) and a title-only override with empty blocks. A document marked out for signature with no fingerprint is refused and must be re-sent; nothing back-fills one. `signing_payload_sha256` is evidence of what was posted, not a control. The send RENDERS the statements from the current rows (`renderDocumentHtml`, shared with the PDF export) — there is no stored artifact to sign, and a render that fails refuses the send — and records `signing_content_fingerprint` (sha256 over the rendered inputs above; sections in the render's own order, sort_order then id), the per-input `signing_input_digests`, and `signing_payload_sha256` (the exact bytes posted). **The fingerprint is taken over what is rendered**: `snapshotRenderInputs` reads the company and brand inputs and fingerprints them in ONE statement, and the render uses those returned values (`renderDocumentHtml({ inputs })`) rather than re-reading the tables. No lock is taken on the company row or its branding — any later edit makes the webhook's recomputation differ and the signature is refused, naming the input; the Signum webhook signs off only from `partner_review`, under the document's row lock, while that fingerprint holds and every mandatory section is still signed off — otherwise it records `signing_refused_reason`, clears the signing state, and leaves the document where it is.
- Review comments are NOT part of what is signed: they stay open while signatures are pending (`lockSectionForWrite(..., { allowWhileSigning: true })`) and close only on a signed-off or filed document.
- A refused signature is quarantined (`afsQuarantinedPdfPath`) and the reason is on the document GET and the review tab; Signum has no void call here, so a person cancels at the provider.
- Every pack that is not signed off or filed is a draft: it is watermarked 'DRAFT — NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION', its email says DRAFT, and it reaches only draft-tier recipients. Drafts reaching draft-tier recipients on a review-required company is deliberate.
- `generateManagementPack` generates `reviewRequired: false` (review SKIPPED) packs as drafts and writes `afs_documents.delivery_withheld_reason`. **`deliverPack` refuses while that column is set** — it is the one place every delivery passes through — and only `signOffDocument` clears it, writing an `audit_log` row. `deliverPack` currently has ONE caller (the deliver route); the scheduler does not deliver (`UnreviewedPackUnavailableError`): a pack with no signatory must not be written to `signed_off`, the status that locks a document. A published status is a follow-up.
- A section's review/sign-off attests to its content. Every section write calls `lockSectionForWrite(companyId, documentId, sectionId)` first — bound to the URL's document, `ReviewError` NOT_FOUND for a section of another document, DOCUMENT_LOCKED for a signed-off/filed one, row lock on section + document — and every content change calls `voidSectionAttestation` before writing: reviewed/signed_off → pending, reviewer and signatory fields cleared, `audit_log` row (`entity_type='afs_section'`, `metadata.event='afs_section_review_invalidated'`). An impersonated session may not void a review. `saveVersion` is a snapshot only and never changes status. `updateAfsSection` needs `updatedBy` to change attested content.

- 2026-09-06: `serverChartSvg.ts` moved in from `services/packs/`. It renders an ECharts option to an SVG STRING because the statutory PDF path goes through WeasyPrint, which runs no JavaScript — so a chart has to arrive already drawn. It registers its own narrow ECharts module set (SVG renderer only) rather than `src/lib/charts/echarts.ts`, which registers the canvas renderer and is client-only, so it is safe to import in a Node request handler. Its only consumer is `pdfExportService.ts`. The default palette still comes from `services/packs/packChartOptions.ts`, so an AFS chart and a pack chart are the same colours.
